answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost.
